name: Gaal
title: The Rebel Against Abimelech
summary: Gaal, son of Ebed, was a man who came to Shechem and incited the city's inhabitants to revolt against Abimelech, the son of Gideon. He sought to exploit the discontent among the Shechemites but was exposed by Zebul, the city's governor, and defeated by Abimelech in battle. His brief appearance illustrates the chaotic period during the time of the judges in Israel.

keyEvents.title: Arrival at Shechem
keyEvents.description: Gaal, son of Ebed, came to Shechem with his brothers and gained the trust of the city's inhabitants, who began to rely on him.

keyEvents.title: Inciting Revolt Against Abimelech
keyEvents.description: During a festival in the temple of their god, Gaal spoke contemptuously about Abimelech and urged the men of Shechem to rise up against his rule.

keyEvents.title: Zebul Warns Abimelech
keyEvents.description: Zebul, the governor of the city, became angry when he heard Gaal's words and secretly sent word to Abimelech about the plans for revolt.

keyEvents.title: Gaal Discovers Abimelech's Army
keyEvents.description: Gaal saw Abimelech's troops approaching from the hills, but Zebul tricked him by claiming they were only shadows of the mountains and tried to delay his reaction.

keyEvents.title: The Defeat Against Abimelech
keyEvents.description: Gaal was forced to go out and fight against Abimelech, but suffered a crushing defeat and was driven into flight. Many of his men fell in battle.

keyEvents.title: Expulsion from Shechem
keyEvents.description: After the defeat, Gaal and his brothers were driven out of Shechem by Zebul, and they lost all influence in the city.
